title: Domain and Range: Interval, Inequality and Set Notation
seo_title: Algebra II Domain and Range Notation Worksheets (TEKS 2A.7I)
standard_text: 2A.7I write the domain and range of a function in interval notation, inequalities, and set notation
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.7I: domain and range in interval notation, inequalities and set notation, domains of rational, square root and log functions. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Three ways to write the same set: inequality x ≥ 2, interval [2, ∞), set notation {x | x ≥ 2}.
  • ( ) means the end is not included; [ ] means it is included. ∞ and −∞ always get ( ).
  • Use ∪ (union) to join pieces: x ≠ 3 is (−∞, 3) ∪ (3, ∞).
  • Domain: a denominator cannot be 0, a square root needs ≥ 0, a log needs > 0.

Examples

Example

Domain of f(x) = 5x − 4

x − 4 ≠ 0, so x ≠ 4

Answer: (−∞, 4) ∪ (4, ∞)

Example

Range of f(x) = 2x − 3

The asymptote is y = −3

The graph is above it

Answer: (−3, ∞)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A bracket for < or >x > 2 is (2, ∞), not [2, ∞).
A bracket next to ∞Always write ∞).
Writing (−∞, ∞) for x ≠ 3Leave out 3: (−∞, 3) ∪ (3, ∞).

faq.a: Write the domain and range of a function in interval notation, inequalities, and set notation.
Union: all numbers in either piece.
The set of all x such that x is greater than 2.
Infinity is not a number you can reach, so it is never included.

items.q: The domain of a function is [−1, 3]. Write it as an inequality.
items.e: ( or ) means the end is not included (< or >); [ or ] means it is included (≤ or ≥). ∞ always gets a parenthesis. −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.

items.q: Write {x | x ≠ −3} in interval notation.
items.e: Every number except −3: all numbers to the left of −3, together (∪) with all numbers to the right. (−∞, −3) ∪ (−3, ∞).

sets.title: Domains of rational, square root and log functions

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log(x + 4) in interval notation?
items.e: A logarithm needs a positive input: x + 4 > 0, so x > −4 (not ≥). (−4, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log(x + 1) in interval notation?
items.e: A logarithm needs a positive input: x + 1 > 0, so x > −1 (not ≥). (−1, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log(x + 9) in interval notation?
items.e: A logarithm needs a positive input: x + 9 > 0, so x > −9 (not ≥). (−9, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x3 − 8x in interval notation?
items.e: A polynomial accepts every real number. (−∞, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x(x − 7)(x − 8) in interval notation?
items.e: The denominator is 0 at x = 7 and x = 8; leave out both. (−∞, 7) ∪ (7, 8) ∪ (8, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x(x − 1)(x − 5) in interval notation?
items.e: The denominator is 0 at x = 1 and x = 5; leave out both. (−∞, 1) ∪ (1, 5) ∪ (5, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x(x − 6)(x − 8) in interval notation?
items.e: The denominator is 0 at x = 6 and x = 8; leave out both. (−∞, 6) ∪ (6, 8) ∪ (8, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = √(−3 − x) in interval notation?
What is the domain of f(x) = log(x − 4) in interval notation?
items.e: A logarithm needs a positive input: x − 4 > 0, so x > 4 (not ≥). (4, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = √(4 − x) in interval notation?
What is the domain of f(x) = √(−7 − x) in interval notation?
What is the domain of f(x) = √(x + 7) in interval notation?
items.e: x + 7 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ −7; the end is included. [−7, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x3 − 7x in interval notation?
items.e: A polynomial accepts every real number. (−∞, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = √(5 − x) in interval notation?
What is the domain of f(x) = log(x − 2) in interval notation?
items.e: A logarithm needs a positive input: x − 2 > 0, so x > 2 (not ≥). (2, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = 1x + 3 in interval notation?
items.e: The denominator x + 3 is 0 when x = −3, so leave out −3. (−∞, −3) ∪ (−3, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x3 − 4x in interval notation?
items.e: A polynomial accepts every real number. (−∞, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log(x + 6) in interval notation?
items.e: A logarithm needs a positive input: x + 6 > 0, so x > −6 (not ≥). (−6, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x3 − 1x in interval notation?
items.e: A polynomial accepts every real number. (−∞, ∞).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x(x + 7)(x − 5) in interval notation?
items.e: The denominator is 0 at x = −7 and x = 5; leave out both. (−∞, −7) ∪ (−7, 5) ∪ (5, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 3x − 1 + 5?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 5: every output except 5. (−∞, 5) ∪ (5, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 3·10x + 7?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 7 and the graph is above it, never on it. (7, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2x + 7?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 7 and the graph is above it, never on it. (7, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −2(x + 6)2 + 1?
items.e: The vertex is (−6, 1) and the parabola opens down. (−∞, 1].

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −3x − 1 − 2?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = −2: every output except −2. (−∞, −2) ∪ (−2, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = √(x + 3) + 3?
items.e: √ is never negative, so the smallest output is 3 (at x = −3). [3, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = √(x + 7) − 4?
items.e: √ is never negative, so the smallest output is −4 (at x = −7). [−4, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −|x + 1| + 5?
items.e: The vertex is (−1, 5) and the V opens down; the vertex is included. {y | y ≤ 5}.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −3|x − 6| − 1?
items.e: The vertex is (6, −1) and the V opens down; the vertex is included. {y | y ≤ −1}.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −3x − 8?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = −8 and the graph is below it, never on it. (−∞, −8).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −1x − 2 − 3?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = −3: every output except −3. (−∞, −3) ∪ (−3, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −2x + 6?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 6 and the graph is below it, never on it. (−∞, 6).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −2·3x + 2?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 2 and the graph is below it, never on it. (−∞, 2).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2x − 6 − 3?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = −3: every output except −3. (−∞, −3) ∪ (−3, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2·3x + 1?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 1 and the graph is above it, never on it. (1, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2x − 6 − 9?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = −9: every output except −9. (−∞, −9) ∪ (−9, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2(x + 7)2 + 5?
items.e: The vertex is (−7, 5) and the parabola opens up. [5, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 3(x + 2)2 + 4?
items.e: The vertex is (−2, 4) and the parabola opens up. [4, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −3·3x + 6?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 6 and the graph is below it, never on it. (−∞, 6).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −3x − 2 − 2?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = −2: every output except −2. (−∞, −2) ∪ (−2, ∞).
